name: Nordic ladder-back side chair
description: A plain Scandinavian-style side chair: four straight legs, a framed seat, three ladder slats between the back posts and low stretchers. Every part is a straight piece of ash.
source: Example design written for Atelier from common side-chair proportions. Not a measured original and not yet checked by a maker.
units: cm; x = side to side, y = up, z = front (+) to back (-)

parts.name: Front leg
parts.note: Mortised on two faces for the front and side aprons.

parts.name: Back post (back leg)
parts.note: One straight piece from floor to top rail, leaning back 2.9°. Mortised for the back apron and slats.

parts.name: Front apron
parts.note: Length includes a 1.5 cm tenon at each end.

parts.name: Back apron
parts.note: Length includes a 1.5 cm tenon at each end.

parts.name: Side apron
parts.note: Length includes a 1.5 cm tenon at each end. Shoulders cut 3° off square to meet the leaning back post.

parts.name: Seat panel
parts.note: Glue up from 2-3 boards. Fix with wooden buttons so it can move across the grain.

parts.name: Back slat
parts.note: Length includes a 1.5 cm tenon at each end.

parts.name: Side stretcher
parts.note: Length includes a 1.5 cm tenon at each end.

parts.name: Front stretcher
parts.note: Length includes a 1.5 cm tenon at each end.

steps.label: Mill all parts flat, square and to size
Mark out every mortise and tenon

needs.why: Marks made on rough, twisted stock aren't square, so every joint inherits the error.
Without layout lines the leaning back post's angled shoulders are a guess.

steps.label: Glue the back frame: posts, back apron and slats

needs.why: Gluing without a dry-fit: a joint that won't close is found with the glue already setting.

steps.label: Glue the front frame: legs, front apron and front stretcher

needs.why: Same as the back: fit first, then glue.

steps.label: Join the frames with the side aprons and side stretchers

needs.why: A loose back frame racks out of square while the side joints set.
A loose front frame racks out of square while the side joints set.

steps.label: Fit the seat panel with wooden buttons

needs.why: There's no frame to fix the seat to yet.
Finish on joint surfaces stops glue from bonding.
